where: Section 2, and worked example steps 4 and 5
problem: The stated rule cannot be followed on this gate. The rule says to find an Euler path on the nMOS graph from VSS to y and on the pMOS graph from VDD to y, but neither path exists for y = ¬(a·b + c). The nMOS graph (nodes VSS, y, n1, edges c:VSS–y, a:y–n1, b:n1–VSS) has every node of even degree, so any Euler trail is closed; the trail given in step 4 starts and ends at VSS. The pMOS graph (c:y–n2, a:n2–VDD, b:n2–VDD) has odd-degree nodes y and n2, so its Euler path must run from y to n2, which is why the step 5 walk ends at n2, not at VDD. A student who tries the stated rule will find no path and think the method is wrong.
fix: State the rule correctly: the Euler path must run between the two nodes of odd degree. If a graph has no odd-degree node, the Euler trail is a closed circuit and the diffusion strip's two ends both contact the same rail (or the same node). Then say in the worked example: the n-strip is VSS–c–y–a–n1–b–VSS, with contacts to the VSS rail at both ends and a contact on the y segment for the output; the p-strip is y–c–n2–a–VDD–b–n2, whose middle segment is VDD (contact to the VDD rail) and whose first and last segments are both n2, joined by a metal line. Both strips are still one continuous strip per side, and the column order c, a, b is unchanged.

problem: "There is no wire crossing in a stick diagram" is false as written. Metal lines routinely cross poly and diffusion with no contact, and that crossing is pure wiring, not a device. Only a poly-diffusion crossing always forms a transistor. A student will read this sentence as a ban on crossing metal over poly or diffusion, which would make routing impossible.
fix: Write: "A poly line crossing diffusion always forms a transistor; poly cannot cross diffusion as plain wiring. Metal crossing poly or diffusion with no contact dot is only a crossing, not a connection."

problem: "Every line thickness becomes a drawn width" is misleading. A stick line has no meaningful thickness; the drawn width comes from the design rules, not from the sketch.
fix: "Each layer line becomes a drawn shape of the width the design rules give, and each gap becomes a spacing from the design rules, all in λ."

problem: The lead lists contact among the layers drawn as a line, then Section 1 says a contact is a dot. The two statements do not match.
fix: In the lead, say a stick diagram uses one line per layer (diffusion, polysilicon, metal) and a dot for each contact.

where: Section 2 and worked example steps 4 and 5
problem: The same rail is called GND in the walks and VSS everywhere else, with no statement that they are the same node. A reader may think two different rails are involved.
fix: Use VSS throughout, or add one line: "GND and VSS here name the same bottom rail."

problem: Chapter 2.6 is referred to in plain text, so on a phone the reader cannot jump to the design-rule chapter.
fix: Link each mention: Chapter 2.6 with the real chapter id for the design rules chapter.
